chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked to buy the garment with a dinar that is not [specified as] a dirham, because it is not known how much of the dirham the dinar is.

key_terms.لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُدْرَى: Because it is not known (indicating uncertainty/gharar)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with dinars without specifying the dirham equivalent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of avoiding gharar (uncertainty) in currency exchange by mandating that a dinar be valued in dirhams to prevent ambiguity in trade. It reflects the early Islamic economic context where dinars (gold) and dirhams (silver) circulated simultaneously, requiring clear parity to ensure fair transactions. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in financial contracts to protect parties from potential exploitation due to fluctuating or undefined exchange rates.
